name: Hebbian Association
description: Activity-dependent synaptic strengthening: cells that fire together wire together. The foundational principle of synaptic plasticity and learning. Implemented via calcium-dependent mechanisms like AMPA receptor insertion and protein synthesis.
key_references: Hebb, D. O. (1949). The Organization of Behavior: A Neuropsychological Theory. Wiley.
Caporale, N., & Dan, Y. (2008). Spike timing-dependent plasticity: a Hebbian learning rule. Annual Review of Neuroscience, 31, 25-46.
empirical_evidence: Direct evidence via voltage clamp recordings, two-photon imaging of spine dynamics, and molecular markers. Long-term potentiation (LTP) is the canonical example. Observed in hippocampus, cortex, cerebellum, and other regions. Underlies memory consolidation and skill learning.

parameters.time_window: tens to hundreds of milliseconds for spike-timing dependence
parameters.learning_rate: varies by synapse type and neuromodulatory state
